items.title: 68516_Gene Ramey oral history interview
items.q: I went up there and played on him, and I tore him up so bad, he got drunk and couldn't play anymore.

ctx.x: He'd see me coming. I went in the Spotlight like last time I did that was right after I went on 52nd Street. He kept on egging me on, you know, because I used to catch him out in the Middle West and tear him up, you know. So he -- he had gotten a name because he made that good record with Hawk, you know, and he was playing the spotlight. He kept on saying, 'Man, you can't play.' He said, I'm going to get you. He said, 'You ain't -- you ain't no bass player.' So I went up there and played. Al Hall remembers that.…

bad, he got drunk and couldn't play anymore. I had to go finish the night for him. So anyway, after that now, he kept soloing and on I didn't. So when I became the house man at Birdland, Joe Jones and I, every night that Pettiford could, he'd come down there with his bass, and he'd go on that side of the bandstand, and I'd take my bass and go right off, you know.
